chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id and Muhammad ibn Ismail, all from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah prohibited the wine, its little and its much, just as He prohibited the dead, the blood, and the flesh of the pig; and the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited from the drinks the intoxicant, and whatever the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has prohibited it.'
And he (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever its much intoxicates, its little is prohibited.'

key_terms.الْمَيْتَة: Dead meat (animal not slaughtered according to ritual law)
key_terms.قَلِيلَهَا وَ كَثِيرَهَا: Its little and its much (small and large quantities)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on small amounts of intoxicants in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the prohibition of wine (khamrah) by equating small and large quantities, a ruling derived from the Prophet's practice which carries divine authority. It articulates the foundational legal maxim (qawaid fiqhiyyah) that 'what intoxicates in large amounts, its small amount is prohibited,' serving as the primary evidence for the total ban on all intoxicants regardless of dosage. This principle underscores the preventative nature of Islamic jurisprudence in preserving the intellect (aql), a key virtue in Shia thought.

en.hubeali: Muhamad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed and Muhammad Bin Ismail, altogether from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Prohibited the wine, a little of it and a lot of it, just as He<sup>azwj</sup> Prohibited the dead, and the blood, and flesh of the swine; and the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> prohibited from drinking the intoxicants, and whatever the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> prohibited, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic has Prohibited it’.
And he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever a lot of it intoxicates, so a little of it is prohibited’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id and Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il all from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Allah has made wine unlawful, regardless of its being a small or large quantity as He has made dead animals, blood and pork unlawful. The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, of drinks, has made intoxicating liquor unlawful. Whatever the Messenger of Allah has made unlawful Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has also made unlawful’,
and he (the Imam) said, ‘Whatever in large quantity is intoxicating liquor, it is unlawful in small quantity also.’”
